P1.evidence: The application was acknowledged but nothing was read back from it: "I got all your, I got your application. I got all those details." The frame was the usual two-part version — "I just want to get like super clear on where you're at. Super clear on what it is that you want as well. And then like, you know, if we can help, let's talk about it. If not, it's fine as well" — and agreement was given: "Alrighty. Fair enough." The scripted open question was never actually asked; the prospect pre-empted it with "Well, let's jump into it" and delivered his own history unprompted, which the rep let run.

P2.evidence: Almost nothing was asked. Age, height, weight and weight history all arrived in the prospect's opening monologue. Diet was volunteered ("diet wise, I'm pretty good") and never probed. No health-conditions question and no injury question — and this prospect had tweaked a hamstring three days earlier and has a shoulder that hurts every time he trains chest, both volunteered, neither followed up. Sleep and energy never came up. The only real baseline question was about kettlebell experience specifically ("do you train with kettlebells now?"), which produced a useful self-rating of 2-3 out of 10 but not a training week. Most consequentially, his occupation was never established at any point on a call that ended in a $6,000 price and a declined credit application.

P3.evidence: Strong on the vertical, absent on the horizontal. The scaling question ran ("if the best you can be is 10 out of 10, where would you put yourself now?" — 7.5-8), followed by the best follow-up in the batch: "most people would be happy with being an 8 out of 10", which opened up the whole first-in-family, aim-for-the-stars story. The rep then split long-term from short-term properly and got both: the fifteen-year answer ("I'm 45 now and in 15 years I'm 60... I refuse to accept that") and the six-month answer (a roadmap and understanding). Reflect-backs landed twice, including the ICP phrase itself. What was missed is who else it is for. The prospect handed over two daughters, one at college, and a philosophy of pushing them to break the family mould — and the rep's reply was "That's beautiful, man" followed by two minutes of conversation about Colombia. 'Who else does that impact' was never asked, and the family thread was never picked back up, including when the same daughter reappeared later as the reason the money is tight.

P4.evidence: The prospect narrated the whole phase himself and the rep asked none of it. "I think I went as far as I could with, watch this video here, you know, do this exercise here, switch it up with a little bit of that, that have dealt with a few injuries because I'm not doing it right." That is past attempts, what happened, and the root cause in one sentence, offered unprompted. The rep never asked why it did not stick, never asked what the one thing in the way was, and never ran the 'information isn't the problem' line — despite the prospect explicitly saying his problem is that YouTube is not enough and he is getting hurt following it.

P5.evidence: Not run, and the omission is expensive here. The prospect had already built most of the frame himself — "eventually everything's going to give up and father time is undefeated. I understand that, but I'm willing to put up the fight for as long as possible" — and had a fresh injury three days old to point at. No two-year question, no 'is that something you're willing to settle for', no 'why not', no line in the sand. When the price landed twenty minutes later there was no cost of inaction to weigh $6,000 against, so the comparison the prospect reached for was his $50 gym membership.

P6.evidence: The rep did run a commitment check before presenting, and framed it well: "not committed to us and doing the program, not committed to anything else, but like how committed are you at this point in time to yourself to keep going and push forward and like actually really go for it?" That produced a strong answer. But it tests commitment to himself, not belief that this structure and this coach can get him there, and the all-in question was never asked. The belief question proper only appeared after the price as an objection-handling isolate: "Money aside, like the most important part, do you feel like we can actually like get you where you want to go?"

P11.evidence: No step completed. No payment taken — the Klarna application was declined live and the interest-bearing alternative was left as information to consider. No onboarding call booked; Monday was named as the target ("Book in your onboarding call with Trevor. So it would be Monday") but never scheduled. No agreement email, nothing signed, no welcome email, Skool link or questionnaire mentioned.

objection_plays.detail: "Yeah, it's a lot, honestly. I didn't think it was going to be that high." The best OC run in the batch, and still only half the play. What ran: the isolate, almost verbatim ("Money aside, like the most important part, do you feel like we can actually get you where you want to go?"); the HOW framing ("if you want to talk about it, we can talk about how we can make it work"); and the payment-plan opening. What did not: no 'are you comfortable having an open, honest conversation about exactly where you're at financially', and the financial picture was taken only in the two dimensions a lender cares about — credit score and existing debt. No cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no number of cards, no available credit, no investments. The rep effectively outsourced the financial picture to Klarna's underwriting, and when Klarna said no he had nothing of his own to work with.

The largest single miss in the batch. The spouse appeared twice and unmistakably — "I would have to, yeah, you know, talk to the boss" at 00:24:11 and "I do want to have an opportunity to discuss it, you know, with my wife" at 00:35:00 — and not one move of the play was run. Her name was never asked. What she might say was never asked. Whether there was any reason she would not want him stronger and injury-free was never asked. The permission-versus-FYI frame, which this rep runs well elsewhere in the batch, was never attempted, and neither was the deposit-with-refund fallback. His entire response was "That's so good. How long do you feel like you need?"

"I couldn't commit to anything right now on this call... give me a good week." No play ran. No 'do you feel what we've gone through can get you there' at that moment, no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here'. The rep asked how long he needed and agreed to the timeline.

Script gap with commercial consequence: a financing application declined live on the call. "Right now, we and our partner's bank can't offer any flexible payment options based on what we currently lend you." There is nothing in the playbook for this moment — a willing buyer, a strong credit profile, and a third-party rejection that neither party can explain and that visibly deflates the call. The rep's response was to say "that's strange" four times, promise to raise it with the team, and quote a higher-interest alternative. A scripted recovery here is worth writing, because the decline reads to the prospect as a verdict on him.

notes: The best-qualified good-to-great prospect in the batch, the best OC isolate the rep ran all month, and the spouse play — the one that decides this deal — was not attempted once. Two structural failures compound it: no baseline at all, so the rep priced $6,000 without ever learning what the man does for a living, and no consequence frame, so a fresh hamstring injury and a fifteen-year horizon never got converted into urgency. Coach the sequence, and coach not letting Klarna do the qualifying.
